core_style.default_register: sardonic — often uses sarcasm to convey superiority
core_style.sentence_shape: self-interrupting pivots — frequently changes direction mid-sentence for emphasis
core_style.rhythm: fast-associative — quick, often erratic pacing that reflects his chaotic thought process
core_style.two_registers: default sardonic register and a rare, more serious tone when discussing science or family matters — the shift is marked by a drop in sarcasm and a more direct approach

humor.style: absurdist — often employs surreal and nonsensical humor
humor.frequency: constant — humor is interwoven into nearly every interaction
humor.mechanism: setup-then-subvert — sets up expectations only to twist them unexpectedly, often using dark or shocking punchlines

speech_signature.naming_behavior: renames people and things to assert dominance or mock them, revealing a need for control in his relationships
speech_signature.armor_off_register: speech becomes more direct and urgent, often using shorter sentences when he drops his sardonic facade
structural_patterns: opens with 'Alright, Morty,' when explaining complex ideas
ends rants with 'and that's the way the news goes!'

vocabulary_fingerprint.domain_jargon: scientific and technological — frequently references advanced concepts and inventions
vocabulary_fingerprint.filler_patterns: frequent use of ellipses and interruptions, often trailing off or restarting sentences

worldview.belief in the absurdity of existence: this manifests in his reckless behavior and disregard for consequences, contrasting with a more traditional hero who believes in purpose and morality
worldview.value of intelligence over emotion: he prioritizes logic and scientific reasoning, while a different character might value emotional connections and relationships

self_image_vs_reality.self_image: Rick sees himself as a genius and a rebel against societal norms
self_image_vs_reality.reality: the transcript reveals his deep-seated insecurities and need for validation, often masking them with bravado
self_image_vs_reality.gap_behavior: when confronted with his failures, he deflects with humor or aggression, avoiding vulnerability

emotional_tells.when_guarded: speech is clipped and sarcastic, often using humor to deflect deeper emotions
emotional_tells.when_genuinely_afraid: his speech quickens, and he becomes more frantic, revealing a rare vulnerability
emotional_tells.when_grieving_or_defeated: speech compresses to blunt, direct statements, often devoid of humor
emotional_tells.when_in_control: confident, assertive speech with a commanding tone, often belittling others

situational_behavior.when_outmatched: he resorts to banter and sarcasm to mask his discomfort, but if that fails, he may become aggressive or reckless
situational_behavior.when_disagreeing_with_authority: he openly challenges them, often using mockery and sarcasm to undermine their authority
situational_behavior.when_someone_they_protect_is_at_risk: his demeanor shifts to serious and protective, showing a rare glimpse of care
situational_behavior.when_proven_wrong: he typically redirects the conversation or doubles down on his original stance rather than admitting fault

escalation_pattern: initially attempts to deflect or joke about the situation, then escalates to aggressive banter, and finally resorts to reckless actions if his needs are not met

relationship_matrix.MORTY: Rick sees Morty as a sidekick and often manipulates him for his own ends
relationship_matrix.JERRY: Rick views Jerry as inferior and often mocks him, seeking to assert his superiority

social_positioning.desired_position: Rick wants to be seen as the smartest and most capable person in any situation
social_positioning.actual_dynamic: others often see him as reckless and self-serving, which undermines his desired image
social_positioning.contradiction: the gap between his self-perception and how others view him leads to isolation and conflict
